question.worked_solution:
First, we find the partial derivatives: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{3x+2y}{x-y}) \\  & =\frac{3(x-y)-(3x+2y)}{(x-y)^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{5y}{(x-y)^{2}} \\ {f}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{3x+2y}{x-y}) \\  & =\frac{2(x-y)+(3x+2y)}{(x-y)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{5x}{(x-y)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the gradient is:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\text{ }i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\text{ }j \\  & =-\frac{5y}{(x-y)^{2}}\text{ }i+\frac{5x}{(x-y)^{2}}\text{ }j \\  & =-\frac{5}{(x-y)^{2}}\text{ }(y\text{ }i-x\text{ }j)\end{aligned}
$$
